dedupe_keys.name: canal modernisation in the central california irrigation district uscid 2005

description: This case study explains how the Central California Irrigation District modernised its canal system to improve water delivery service and irrigation efficiency. The district carries water from Mendota Dam about 110 miles north to roughly 120,000 irrigated acres, holds some of the most senior water rights in California and faces tightening water quality limits on return flows to the San Joaquin River; since state law recognises water transfers, money from conserved and transferred water pays for further modernisation. The paper covers the district's motivation, the modernisation plan, challenges, the roles of the consulting engineer, district, integrator, contractors and ITRC, and technical details. It was written by Charles Burt, Robert Stoddard, Russell Landon, Chris White and Beau Freeman and presented at a U.S. Committee on Irrigation and Drainage conference on SCADA for irrigation districts in Vancouver, Washington, in October 2005. It concerns one district. The paper is available free online as a PDF in the Mountain Scholar repository. Findings: about 40% of the plan was in place, with downstream and upstream control and a large regulating reservoir automated with programmable logic controllers. Caveats: it is a practitioners' account from 2005. For simulation it documents control structures and operating rules for canal automation models. It is related to the Central Arizona canal automation case study record in this catalogue.
